name: SIMS
aliases: Single-Incision Mini-Slings versus Standard Midurethral Slings
question: In women undergoing primary sling surgery for stress-predominant urinary incontinence, are adjustable anchored single-incision mini-slings noninferior to standard midurethral slings for patient-reported improvement?

arms.label: Adjustable anchored single-incision mini-sling (Ajust or Altis)
standard retropubic or transobturator tension-free midurethral sling

design.population: Women aged 18 years or older with predominant stress urinary incontinence after failed or declined conservative treatment; no previous SUI surgery, stage 2 or greater anterior/apical prolapse, or planned concomitant surgery.
design.locator: NEJM pp 1231-1233, Methods and Figure 1; HTA scientific summary p iv

verdictNote: Patient-reported improvement met the 10-point margin; dyspareunia and additional surgery were more frequent with mini-slings.
takeaway: Adjustable anchored Ajust or Altis single-incision mini-slings were noninferior to standard retropubic or transobturator midurethral slings for patient-reported improvement at 15 months (79.1% versus 75.6%; adjusted risk difference 4.6 percentage points, 95% CI −2.7 to 11.8).

reports.label: Primary clinical report through 36 months
reports.citation: Abdel-Fattah M, Cooper D, Davidson T, et al. Single-Incision Mini-Slings for Stress Urinary Incontinence in Women. *N Engl J Med.* 2022;386(13):1230-1243.
reports.followUp: Primary endpoint at 15 months after randomization (approximately 1 year after surgery); follow-up through 36 months after randomization.
